Detailed Description

Dynamic chained hashtable.

This hashtable resizes dynamically. It starts with the minimal size of 16 buckets. It doubles the size when it reaches a load factor greater than or equal to 0.5 and it halves the size when the load factor is less than or equal to 0.125.

All the elements are reallocated in a single resize operation done inside tommy_hashdyn_insert() or tommy_hashdyn_remove().

Note that the resize operation takes approximately 100 [ms] with 1 million elements, and 1 [second] with 10 million elements. This could be a problem in real-time applications.

The resize also fragments the heap, as it involves allocating a double-sized table, copying elements, and deallocating the older table, leaving a big hole in the heap.

The tommy_hashlin hashtable fixes both problems.

To initialize the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashdyn_init().

tommy_hashdyn hashdyn;
tommy_hashdyn_init(&hashdyn);

tommy_hashdyn_init
TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_init(tommy_hashdyn *hashdyn)
Initializes the hashtable.

To insert elements in the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashdyn_insert() for each element. In the insertion call you have to specify the address of the node, the address of the element, and the hash value of the key to use. The address of the element is used to initialize the tommy_node::data field of the node, and the hash to initialize the tommy_node::index field.

struct element {
int value;
// other fields
tommy_node node;
};
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element)); // creates the element
elem->value = ...; // initializes the element
tommy_hashdyn_insert(&hashdyn, &elem->node, elem, tommy_inthash_u32(elem->value)); // inserts the element

To find an element in the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashdyn_search() providing a comparison function, its argument, and the hash of the key to search.

int compare(const void* arg, const void* elem)
{
return *(const int*)arg != ((const struct element*)elem)->value;
}
int value_to_find = 1;
struct element* elem = tommy_hashdyn_search(&hashdyn, compare, &value_to_find, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_find));
if (!elem) {
// not found
} else {
// found
}

To iterate over all the elements in the hashtable with the same key, you have to use tommy_hashdyn_bucket() and follow the tommy_node::next pointer until 0. You have also to check explicitly for the key, as the bucket may contain different keys.

int value_to_find = 1;
tommy_node* i = tommy_hashdyn_bucket(&hashdyn, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_find));
while (i) {
struct element* elem = i->data; // gets the element pointer
if (elem->value == value_to_find) {
printf("%d\n", elem->value); // process the element
}
i = i->next; // goes to the next element
}

To remove an element from the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashdyn_remove() providing a comparison function, its argument, and the hash of the key to search and remove.

struct element* elem = tommy_hashdyn_remove(&hashdyn, compare, &value_to_remove, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_remove));
if (elem) {
free(elem); // frees the element allocated memory
}

To destroy the hashtable you have to remove all the elements, and deinitialize the hashtable calling tommy_hashdyn_done().

tommy_hashdyn_done
TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_done(tommy_hashdyn *hashdyn)
Deinitializes the hashtable.

If you need to iterate over all the elements in the hashtable, you can use tommy_hashdyn_foreach() or tommy_hashdyn_foreach_arg(). For traversal that permits insertions and removals, use tommy_hashdyn_head() and tommy_hashdyn_next(), or tommy_hashdyn_tail() and tommy_hashdyn_prev(). Hashes are compared from the least significant bit to the most significant bit, with 0 before 1. Equal hashes are visited in insertion order. This order is independent of the number of buckets and progressive resizing. It differs from the bucket order used by foreach and to_list.

Iterators are pointers to nodes currently contained in the hashtable. Inserting elements or removing other nodes does not invalidate them or change the relative iteration order of the remaining elements. A forward or backward traversal visits every original element that remains contained, even if removals cause the table to shrink or insertions grow it. New elements can be visited if inserted after the current position in the traversal direction; elements inserted before it need not be visited.

Removing the pointed node invalidates its use as an iterator, even if its storage has not been freed. Obtain the next or previous node before removal, and keep that saved node contained until continuing the traversal.

tommy_hashdyn_node* i = tommy_hashdyn_head(&hashdyn);
while (i) {
tommy_hashdyn_node* next = tommy_hashdyn_next(&hashdyn, i);
if (should_remove(i->data)) {
free(tommy_hashdyn_remove_existing(&hashdyn, i));
}
i = next;
}

Removes an element from the hashtable.

Changing a hash with tommy_hashdyn_rehash_existing() can change iteration order, so the traversal guarantee does not cover rehashing during traversal. After swapping containers, use the container that now contains the node. Clearing or deinitializing the container invalidates all its iterators. Concurrent traversal and modification require external synchronization.

Iterator calls scan bucket contents without allocating or modifying memory. With a good hash function and normal dynamic resizing, a full traversal runs in expected O(n) time. Under the same hash distribution assumption, sparse tables require expected O(n + b) time, where n is the number of elements and b is the number of buckets. Such tables can arise after tommy_hashdyn_reserve(), tommy_hashdyn_clear(), or tommy_hashdyn_to_list(). In pathological cases with severe hash collisions, traversal can take O(n^2 + b) time. Use foreach for guaranteed O(n + b) traversal when no insertions or removals are needed.

◆ tommy_hashdyn_swap()

void tommy_hashdyn_swap ( tommy_hashdyn *  first,
tommy_hashdyn *  second 
)

Exchanges the complete state of two initialized hashtables, including bucket allocations.

The hashtables must not share nodes. Nodes and elements are not accessed or modified. Existing node pointers remain valid and belong to the other hashtable. Passing the same hashtable twice has no effect. Both hashtables remain usable and deinitializable.

Parameters
firstThe first hashtable.
secondThe second hashtable.
Note
This operation is O(1) with respect to the number of elements.

◆ tommy_hashdyn_clear()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_clear ( tommy_hashdyn *  hashdyn)

Removes all elements, preserving the allocated buckets.

Call tommy_hashdyn_shrink() after clearing to restore the initial capacity. The hashtable remains initialized and can be reused immediately. Elements are not freed and nodes are not accessed or modified. Their links must not be used to traverse the previous contents. You can call this function after tommy_hashdyn_foreach() has freed the elements. Subsequent insertions and removals retain the normal resizing policy.

Parameters
hashdynThe hashtable.
Note
This operation is O(b), where b is the number of buckets.

◆ tommy_hashdyn_reserve()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_reserve ( tommy_hashdyn *  hashdyn,
tommy_size_t  count 
)

Pre-allocates buckets for the specified number of elements.

It ensures that the hashtable has enough buckets allocated to contain the specified number of elements without triggering a dynamic resize on insertion. Subsequent removals retain the normal shrinking policy and may reduce the allocated capacity.

Parameters
hashdynThe hashtable.
countNumber of elements to reserve space for.

◆ tommy_hashdyn_shrink()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_shrink ( tommy_hashdyn *  hashdyn)

Shrinks the allocated buckets to fit the current number of elements.

The target is the smallest power of 2, at least 16, for which the number of elements is strictly less than half the number of buckets. If the current allocation is already no larger than the target, nothing is done. An empty hashtable is reduced to 16 buckets. Elements are not freed, and the tommy_node::data and tommy_node::index fields are left unchanged. The order of elements with the same hash is preserved.

Parameters
hashdynThe hashtable.
Note
This operation is O(b), where b is the previous number of buckets.

Inserts an element only if no equal element is already contained.

If found, the first equal element is returned, and the hashtable and candidate node are left unchanged. Otherwise, the candidate is inserted using the normal insertion policy, and data is returned. Elements are not freed by this call.

hashHash of the candidate key, consistent with the comparison function.
Returns
The first equal element, or data if the candidate was inserted.

◆ tommy_hashdyn_rehash_existing()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_rehash_existing ( tommy_hashdyn *  hashdyn,
tommy_hashdyn_node *  node,
tommy_hash_t  hash 
)

Updates the hash of an element already contained in the hashtable.

The node must belong to this hashtable. The caller updates the element key and provides its new hash, without modifying tommy_node::index directly. If the hash is unchanged, the node and its position are left unchanged. Otherwise, the node is moved to the tail of the destination bucket, even if the old and new hashes identify the same bucket. The tommy_node::data field and the number of elements are left unchanged. No memory allocation, deallocation or resize is performed. Equal keys are allowed; no uniqueness check is performed.

Parameters
hashdynThe hashtable.
nodeThe node whose hash is updated.
hashThe new hash of the element.
Note
This operation is O(1).

◆ tommy_hashdyn_foreach()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_foreach ( tommy_hashdyn *  hashdyn,
tommy_foreach_func *  func 
)

Calls the specified function for each element in the hashtable.

You cannot add or remove elements from the inside of the callback, but can use it to deallocate them.

tommy_hashdyn hashdyn;
// initializes the hashtable
tommy_hashdyn_init(&hashdyn);
...
// creates an element
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element));
...
// insert it in the hashtable
tommy_hashdyn_insert(&hashdyn, &elem->node, elem, tommy_inthash_u32(elem->value));
...
// deallocates all the elements iterating the hashtable
tommy_hashdyn_foreach(&hashdyn, free);
// deallocates the hashtable
tommy_hashdyn_done(&hashdyn);

If the callback frees the elements, the hashtable retains dangling node pointers. Call tommy_hashdyn_clear() before reusing it, or tommy_hashdyn_done() to release its storage.

Parameters
hashdynThe hashtable.
funcFunction to call with each element.

◆ tommy_hashdyn_to_list()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashdyn_to_list ( tommy_hashdyn *  hashdyn,
tommy_list *  list 
)

Transfers all elements from the hashtable into a tommy_list.

Removes every element from the hashdyn hashtable and inserts them into the provided list (at the tail), preserving the per-bucket order but not guaranteeing any particular global order.

After the call:

  • the hashtable is left empty and initialized, preserving its allocated buckets
  • the target list contains all the elements that were previously in the hashtable

The tommy_node::data and tommy_node::index fields are left unchanged.

This function is useful when you need to:

  • extract all elements to process/sort them outside the hashtable
  • convert the hashtable into a list for sequential iteration
  • prepare for a full clear + re-insertion with different hash/ordering
  • move ownership of the nodes to a list-based container

Typical usage pattern:

tommy_list all_elements;
tommy_list_init(&all_elements);
// move everything out of the hashtable into the list
tommy_hashdyn_to_list(&hashdyn, &all_elements);
// now you can sort, filter, process sequentially, etc.
tommy_list_sort(&all_elements, compare_by_value);

Transfers all elements from the hashtable into a tommy_list.

tommy_list_sort
TOMMY_API void tommy_list_sort(tommy_list *list, tommy_compare_func *cmp)
Sorts a list.
Parameters
hashdynThe hashtable to drain.
listThe destination list. It must be initialized and must not share nodes with the hashtable. Existing elements remain at the head of the list.
Note
This operation is O(b), where b is the number of buckets.
No memory allocation or deallocation is performed.
The relative order of elements that were in the same bucket is preserved, but the order among different buckets is bucket-order dependent.
